title: Wrong Mugshot
briefing: Two services were rolled out this morning and neither has a single running pod. evidence-api is stuck on its first start. badge-scanner is stuck too, for a completely different reason. Ops left a handover note (case/registry-note.txt). Both pods should be up, and both images must be the ones the registry actually has.
objective: Get evidence-api (2 pods) and badge-scanner (1 pod) running.
hints: Look at what the pods say about themselves: the status column is not the whole story, and the events say which image could not be pulled and why.
evidence-api: 'not found' means the registry has no such tag. Read the tag in the Deployment and compare it with the release in the handover note, character by character.
badge-scanner: 'authorization failed' means the registry wants a login. A docker-registry Secret holds one, and the pod template must name it under imagePullSecrets.
`kubectl set image` fixes a tag; `kubectl create secret docker-registry` plus `kubectl patch deployment` adds the pull secret.

findings.clue: evidence-api cannot pull registry.example.com/evidence:2.4.l: 'not found' means that tag does not exist. The release is 2.4.1, with a digit one at the end, not a letter L.
badge-scanner's image exists but the registry refuses the pull: 'authorization failed'. It needs credentials, passed as an image pull secret.
The handover note has the release (2.4.1) and the login for the private registry.
